flags: Instrument flow chart occupies PDF p.15-16 (printed -7- and -8-), header verbatim "(2) INSTRUMENT".

Flow-chart pages have an empty text layer; all boxes/arrows were read from the page raster (base image + SMask composited over white) — the raw extracted image without its SMask renders as unreadable black blobs.

NO green boxes / green outlines anywhere in the Instrument chart (verified by pixel scan of both pages: 0 green pixels). No solo candidates and no first solo in this category — the mission table on PDF p.191 lists DUAL only, 14 sorties / 18,4 h.
RED label text = night. Pixel scan: 0 red pixels on PDF p.15; exactly one red band on PDF p.16 (y 222-239) covering both "I 3601" and "I 4701". No other night items in Instrument.

I 3601 is drawn with the single-thin ground-style border and sits in the LEFT column of PDF p.16 (below CO 109), unlike the thick F/S border of I 3501-I 3504. It is nevertheless a simulator sortie: PDF p.156 gives "TRAINING SECTION: I36XX SORTIES/HOURS TOTAL: 1/1,3 MISSIONS: Night IFR Navigation. DEVICE: OFT/FTD/PTT". Recorded band "fs"; printed border anomaly flagged.

PRINTING INCONSISTENCY: the I 4502 -> I 4601 page-break connector is SOLID where it leaves I 4502 on PDF p.15 but DASHED where it enters I 4601 on PDF p.16. Measured at 8x, the p.15 stub is one unbroken 59.5 pt ink run while the p.16 stub is 8 dashes separated by ~1 pt gaps. The two stubs are NOT at the same page x: the whole p.16 drawing is placed 35.5 pt further LEFT than p.15's (placed image bbox x0 = 92.2 pt on p.15 vs 56.7 pt on p.16, both 447.9 pt wide), so every column carries that shift — flight column x 262.1-363.8 -> 226.6-328.2, ground column x 94.0-195.8 -> 58.5-158.8, F/S column x 432.6-533.8 -> 397.1-498.2. Both page-break stubs carry the identical 35.5 pt offset (flight stub centre x 312.9 -> 277.4; dashed I 4501 -> CO 109 stub x 144.4 -> 108.4), which is what makes the stub pairing unambiguous.
I 4701 is printed BETWEEN I 4602 and I 4603 in the flight column, exactly as the Special Instructions require (I4701 before I4603).

The F/S column is drawn as five DISCONNECTED groups on PDF p.15-16: no arrow exists between I 3201 and I 3202, between I 3203 and I 3301, between I 3304 and I 3401, or between I 3404 and I 3501. Each group only feeds the flight column. Verified at 5x zoom on every gap; no edges invented across them.
GPS feeds the flight column via a T-junction on the I 4490 -> I 4501 trunk rather than its own arrowhead.
C 4791 (Contact first solo) appears as a dashed-bordered cross-category reference box at the head of the Instrument flight column; the arrow it sends into I 4101 is solid.

Sortie counts cross-checked against the syllabus section tables: I31XX 2 (p.151), I32XX 3 (p.152), I33XX 4 (p.153), I34XX 4 (p.154), I35XX 4 (p.155), I36XX 1 (p.156) = 18 F/S boxes; flight mission table p.191 I41XX 2 + I42XX 2 + I43XX 2 + I4490 1 + I45XX 2 + I46XX 3 + I4701 1 + I4890 1 = 14 flight boxes. Both match the drawn box counts exactly.
Box-style taxonomy measured from border pixel widths: thick single = F/S, double thin = flight, single thin = ground/academic, dashed double = cross-category reference.

"ground_links" is an extra array beyond the requested schema, added so that no printed arrow is lost: it holds the ground-to-ground academic chain plus the sortie-to-ground dashed arrow I 4501 -> CO 109.
Section designators are written with Latin X (I41XX); the syllabus text on PDF p.191 mixes Greek capital Chi and Latin X in the same table.

COLUMN ORDER is printed left -> right as ground/academic | flight | F/S, the same arrangement as the sibling vfr_navigation.json. It is recorded per sortie in "column" because it CANNOT be inferred from the order of the "sorties" array: that array lists the whole "fs" band before the whole "flights" band, which is the reverse of the printed left-to-right order. Measured column x-ranges (page points): PDF p.15 ground 94.0-195.8, flight 262.1-363.8, F/S 432.6-533.8; PDF p.16 ground 58.5-158.8, flight 226.6-328.2, F/S 397.1-498.2 (the whole p.16 drawing is offset 35.5 pt to the left). The single exception is I 3601, printed in the GROUND column of p.16 although it is an F/S sortie - see its note.

Field "diagram_level" is the vertical row index of the printed chart: boxes drawn at the same height share a level. Because the Instrument chart spans two pages the numbering runs CONTINUOUSLY, levels 1-15 on PDF p.15 and levels 16-20 on PDF p.16; it is not restarted per page. Levels 1, 5, 8, 9 and 13 hold no flight box and levels 1, 5 and 20 hold no F/S box, which is why the per-band level sequences have gaps. The full level map, including the ground boxes and the dashed cross-reference box C 4791 (level 3), is in "diagram_levels"; within a level the entries are listed left to right: ground/cross-ref column, centre flight column, right F/S column.

Field "box_style" records the PRINTED border/fill measured from the raster, using the same vocabulary as vfr_navigation.json: "thick_solid_black" = 2.38-2.50 pt single border (F/S), "double_outline_black" = two ~0.9-1.0 pt concentric borders 1.44 pt apart (flight), "orange_fill_black_border" = the check rides I 4490 / I 4890, plus "thin_solid_black" = 1.00 pt single border, used only by I 3601 and matching the ground/academic boxes. box_style is therefore NOT a restatement of "band": I 3601 is band "fs" but box_style "thin_solid_black", and I 4490 / I 4890 are band "flights" but box_style "orange_fill_black_border".

CAVEAT on the inherited value name "orange_fill_black_border": it is kept for parity with vfr_navigation.json, but it understates the printed border on BOTH files. Measured at 16x, I 4490 and I 4890 carry exactly the same DOUBLE outline as the plain flight boxes (two ~0.94 pt lines 1.44 pt apart on each edge) with fill RGB(255,192,0) added, not a single border; the same 4-line construction was measured on N 4690 at PDF p.19 (y 682.12 / 683.56 and 701.81 / 703.25), the box that vfr_navigation.json labels with this value. The distinguishing feature of the value is the check-ride FILL, not the border. A renderer should draw check rides as a double outline plus orange fill in both categories.
legend_observed "border_double_thin" cites I 4890 as an example of the flight-box border; that is correct and was re-verified at 16x — I 4890 is double-outlined despite its orange fill.
